newsitem.title: USA: Phone firm officials testify at Okla. bomb trial.
newsitem.headline: Phone firm officials testify at Okla. bomb trial.

text.p: Telephone company officials took the stand in the Oklahoma City bombing trial Wednesday, bringing records of calls prosecutors claim were made by alleged bomber Timothy McVeigh.
Security investigators from New York-based NYNEX and General Telephone Co. appeared briefly with their company records.

Government prosecutors claim McVeigh made numerous calls on a telephone calling card bearing the name Daryl Bridges when he planned the bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah federal building in Oklahoma City on April 19, 1995, that killed 168 people.
McVeigh has pleaded not guilty to planning and carrying out the bombing. If convicted, he faces the death penalty.

Under cross-examination, the telephone company officials said they could only tell the number from which a call was made and the number that was called, but not who made the call or what was said during it.
